title: Maester 3.0 due 1 December: check your pipelines now
summary: Maester co-creator Merill Fernando said on 25 November 2026 that Maester 3.0 is coming out on 1 December; the project's releases page still shows 3.0 as a preview. Per the official upgrade guide, 3.0 gives Maester its own test engine: built-in tests ship inside the module instead of being copied into a tests folder, PowerShell 7.4 or later is required (Windows PowerShell 5.1 is no longer supported), and Pester becomes optional (needed, 5.7.1 or later, only for Pester-format custom tests or scripts that call New-PesterConfiguration). Disabling built-in tests moves to maester-config.json, built-in test Block and Tag values in results change, and CI test history for built-in tests restarts because test names change. The guide says to remove old Maester versions before installing 3.x.
why: Many tenants run Maester unattended in GitHub Actions or Azure DevOps. A pipeline that installs the latest version will pick up 3.0 and can break on 5.1 runners, missing Pester or result parsers that read Tag/Block.
todo: Do now: pin the Maester version in automation until you have tested 3.0.
Move runners to PowerShell 7.4 or later and install Pester 5.7.1+ yourself if you keep Pester-format custom tests.
Run your usual command with -DryRun -PassThru on the preview and compare results with 2.x.
Update dashboards or parsers that rely on Tag or Block of built-in tests.
effective_note: Release date 1 Dec 2026 per the maintainer's post on X (announced, not yet released). Changes per maester.dev upgrade guide (3.0 preview).

sources.title: Merill Fernando on X (25 Nov 2026): Maester 3.0 coming out on 1 Dec
